note: Inherited requirements with explicitly bounded source mappings. Mapping is not full language conformance. SCHEMA 2 (card T00-CT-SCHEMA, T00.1-T00.9): every per-case stage entry is an object whose status is derived from named executed evidence, not a host-unconditional string. An `executed` entry must name the `executor` (a pinned runner in compiler/tests/ct_corpus.rs), the `artifact` that runner reads (the case's own fixture), an `observations` count of runner invocations, and, where the runner is host-gated, the exact `host_gate` list of target_os values on which it runs; the harness recomputes all of that from its own dispatch and refuses any drift, so on a host outside the gate the entry reads as unexecuted instead of inheriting `executed`. Statuses are `executed`, `recorded_not_gated` (an archived transcript that no workspace test re-runs; it must carry a `record` pointer and can never be counted as executed), `not_applicable` (the stage is structurally absent for this route, or the case's own refusal provably never reaches it) and `unassessed`. `proof` is never `not_applicable`, because a bound theorem could be added for any case. `native_sanitized` is `not_applicable` on a route that has no `c_emission` stage and `unassessed` everywhere else: card T08-SRC-CT deliberately narrowed the earlier universal rule when the check-only `epoch` route landed, because there is nothing to sanitize where nothing is emitted, and the route vocabulary — not the case — decides it. SCHEMA 1's `cfg` and `type_checker` are gone: they conflated four real passes and their reading differed per route. The stage vocabulary now names the passes that exist (parse, elaborate, task_lowering, task_ledger_check, mutex_lowering, mutex_invariant_check, epoch_lowering, epoch_bound_check, sequential_whole_program, sequential_reference_execution, task_reference_execution, mutex_reference_execution, c_emission, native_execution, native_sanitized, legacy_c_twin, proof) and each case declares its `route`. A route's possible stages are listed under stage_vocabulary.routes; every stage outside them is structurally absent for that route. The task route (ScopedCopyTasksV1/ScopedOwnedTasksV1 and its ScopedReadSharesV1/ScopedErrorPayloadV1 extensions) builds a checked task IR, which is what schema 1's `cfg` meant there; the source.mutex.guard.v1 route (CT26/CT27/CT28/CT29/CT30/CT31/CT32/CT33/CT48) emits directly from a checked event list and has no CFG stage at all, which schema 1 could only express as `cfg: unassessed`. The source.epoch.bound.v1 route (CT35/CT36/CT38/CT39, cards T08-EPOCH-SRC and T08-SRC-CT) lowers a lexical epoch declaration onto the unedited FlatEpochBoundV1 checker and is check-only: an admitted epoch is a checked accounting statement about declared shapes, published with c_source: None and reference_observation: None, so it has no reference-execution, emission, native or sanitized stage at all. The legacy_c route (CT43/CT45, card CT-CTWIN; CT40, wave-17 CT lane) is the first non-QCore artifact in this corpus: all three cases name C constructs — a registration API that defers a callback past its own return, a destructor whose body is outside the translation unit, and a store of an owned pointer into an object that outlives the call — that no QCore syntax expresses, so the case's artifact is a C twin run through the real unrestricted-C gateway. On that route `parse` is the gateway's own C admission (validate_unrestricted_c11: Clang preprocessing plus syntax acceptance of the case's own .c bytes) and `legacy_c_twin` is analyze_unrestricted_c11's resource projection and unit verdict; there is no `elaborate` because there is no QCore source, and no emission, native or sanitized stage because the gateway analyzes C rather than producing any. The evidence is the whole verdict — unit result, verbatim withdrawal reason, complete per-function status map and complete ordered diagnostic inventory, each rebuilt from the analysis and compared wholesale — plus controls that remove exactly the construct the scenario names, at least one of which the gateway must check, so a recorded Unknown is never merely `the projection cannot express this at all`. That route's stages are gated on Clang rather than on a target_os, which the stage record carries as a new optional `tool_gate` beside `host_gate`; the derived summary reports it as a separate `tool_scope` axis, because a stage that reads `host_gate: null` and needs Clang would otherwise be read as having run wherever the tests ran. A control that varies only the declared contracts re-analyzes the case's own artifact and is therefore counted as a further observation of that case's own stage, which is the one deliberate exception to `a control is never the case's own stage`. CT40 joins that route in wave 17, after card CTWIN-PUBLISH closed the gateway hazard that had left it unmapped: a store of a tracked identity into a static-storage object was Safe with no diagnostic, so wave 9 could record no verdict of the class the scenario demands. It is now refused, and the case maps with three controls rather than one, because two of them are pinned for NOT moving the verdict. Removing `_Atomic` alone changes not one measured byte — the projection derives no atomicity or synchronization fact, so it cannot — and removing the release instead is still refused, with one diagnostic rather than two. The mapping therefore rests on the construct the case's `expected` text names, the publication protocol, and explicitly not on atomicity or on the `prematurely freed` half of its title, neither of which this projection decides. The sequential route carries its first mapped cases in wave 26 (card CT-WIRE-LANE): CT06 and CT11, whose artifact is a source.string.v1 module. Card STRING-CONCAT's `borrow_utf8` bridge is this corpus's first LOCAL shared alias - an immutable view of an owned std.buffer's own bytes, bound in the same frame, with no task and no second party - which is exactly the form the wave-3 CT lane recorded as missing when it left CT11 unmapped, and its row in that lane's record is retired by declaration rather than edited. cases.scenario: Move an owned buffer to child; child returns it; parent joins and drops
cases.semantic_profile: ScopedOwnedTasksV1: actual own<Buffer> affine move/return with root allocation, immutable i32 payload and payload-free errors. Linux native allocation, pointer-preserving child return, creator join and exactly-once parent drop agree with reference execution. Loans, general owned graphs, owned errors and native runtime refinement proofs remain open.

cases.scenario: Parent uses buffer after successful move capture
cases.semantic_profile: ScopedOwnedTasksV1: actual own<Buffer> affine move/return with root allocation, immutable i32 payload and payload-free errors. The parent read after successful move rejects at Q600; CT01 supplies the accepted native control. Failed creation retains the original parent binding. Loans, general owned graphs, owned errors and native runtime refinement proofs remain open.

cases.scenario: Parent and child share reads with complementary positive shares
cases.semantic_profile: ScopedReadSharesV1: one owned Buffer lent to two children with complementary halves of the 1024-unit read authority, both reading it while the parent also reads it, and Buffer writes on either side of the lending window because a write demands reconstructed exclusive authority. Executed from the fixture: parse, elaborate, lower, all-paths task-IR check, reference execution, C11 emission, and three fixed Linux schedules whose emitted C runs under ASan/UBSan/LSan with a heap witness recording every Buffer by address - one object allocated and released exactly once across two live borrowers, a refused second creation returning only its own share, and a refused join returning none and reclaiming nothing. The complementary refusals are mapped as CT04 and CT05. This is not evidence about arbitrary schedules, other targets or the C memory model; ThreadSanitizer does not intercept C11 thrd_create, so data-race freedom rests on the checker's no-write-while-shared rule. The lending budget is over authority handed out, not a separation-logic fraction; disjoint slicing, write shares, more than two readers, byte accounting and nested workers stay refused.

cases.scenario: Parent writes while child retains a read share
cases.semantic_profile: ScopedReadSharesV1: the parent writes its Buffer while both children still hold their halves. Refused with the exact single-entry cascade [Q600] carrying LoanOutstanding { resource: 1, outstanding: 1024, borrowers: [2, 3] }, which names the outstanding total and every borrower rather than the bare fact of a loan. An accepted Linux control moves the same write after both joins, so the refusal is keyed to the outstanding shares and not to writing at all. A rejection carries no execution post-state, so only parse and check are executed.

cases.scenario: Two children each request FULL for the same memory
cases.semantic_profile: ScopedReadSharesV1: two children each request the whole read authority for one allocation. Refused with the exact single-entry cascade [Q600] carrying ShareExceedsAuthority { resource: 1, outstanding: 1024, requested: 1024 }; the excess request is refused as a whole and the outstanding total is unchanged. An accepted Linux control lends 511 and 513 of the same allocation, so the budget boundary is a boundary rather than a blanket refusal of two borrowers. A rejection carries no execution post-state, so only parse and check are executed.

cases.scenario: Same pointer copied into differently named variables
cases.semantic_profile: StandardStringV1: an immutable UTF-8 {ptr, len} view of an owned std.buffer's own bytes, copied into a second name by a whole-extent slice ({ptr = p + 0, len = 2 - 0}), inside one flat sequential entry. The obligation the original carries is measured to follow the copy: the release names the copy, not the view it was taken from. Owning copies, mutable aliases, aliases crossing a function or a thread, and pointer values the language gives no type remain outside this route.

cases.scenario: Two disjoint array halves mutated independently
cases.semantic_profile: ScopedWriteLeasesV1 with card WRITE-LEND-TASKS' range write lease and card WRITE-LEND-TASKS-EXERCISE's worker-body byte write, remapped by card CT07-TWO-THREAD-REMAP (wave 37) from the sequential write lend card CT07-WRITE-REMAP (wave 30) mapped, which had itself remapped the read-loan program the wave-28 lane mapped: two WRITE authorities over disjoint ranges of one allocation's int32_t payload - lend buffer 0..2 and lend buffer 2..4 - held by TWO THREADS, each worker writing a byte through its own lease in its own body, the owner reading both bytes back only after both joins, which is when the leases return. Each worker writes its own RELATIVE byte 0 and the events name owner bytes 0 and 2, so the rebasing law is visible in the observation rather than asserted about it. Disjointness is decided at check time by ownership::axes_overlap, called by LeaseRange::overlaps in the scoped-task ledger, and the exclusivity is the ledger's rather than a route rule's: a second overlapping lease refuses at the spawn site before anything is emitted. WHAT MOVED, and it is the scenario's own word: wave 30's two write authorities were bindings of ONE SEQUENTIAL ENTRY - 'NOT two threads', as that card's own semantic profile said, naming WRITE-LEND-TASKS as the residual; that residual's successor landed in wave 31 and was made exercisable in wave 36, so 'independently' now means two threads writing distinct bytes of one object under ASan/UBSan/LSan with the native observation compared line for line against the reference execution of the checked task IR, and the single allocation checked by address. WHAT DID NOT MOVE: no count - CT07 was mapped before this card and is mapped after it, so this is evidence quality and not coverage (constraint 23). Boundaries, stated rather than left silent: the payload is one int32_t, so the two halves are two bytes each (BUFFER_PAYLOAD_BYTES = 4; residual WRITE-LEND-TASKS-EXTENT); there is NO ThreadSanitizer evidence, because TSan cannot run any program this route emits, lease or not (residual TASK-ROUTE-TSAN-SEGV, measured on three programs in wave 36), so 'two threads write distinct memory locations without a race' is carried by C11 3.14 plus the sanitizer and allocation-identity evidence and NOT by a race detector; and proof stays unassessed, since wave 31's and wave 36's Lean theorems are about the model's authorities and writes and are not bound to this artifact by a named test (residual CT07-TWO-THREAD-PROOF-LEG). Bounds are split across the two layers that own them: past_range_byte.qcore refuses a real payload byte at the LEASE it goes through, and past_extent_read.qcore refuses a real owner access at the PAYLOAD's extent. Disjointness is overlapping_leases.qcore's OverlappingLeases refusal naming both ranges. Wave 30's sequential program is retained as the sequential_write_halves accept control and wave 28's read-loan program as the read_loan accept control, with wave 30's three sequential reject twins retained as rejection controls, so this remap is a strict superset of the evidence wave 30 published rather than a swap.

cases.scenario: Overlapping array ranges
cases.semantic_profile: StandardStringV1 with card CT07-SLICE-PERMISSIONS's range-wise exclusion, taking the REJECT arm of the case's expected text: a write whose one-byte range [1, 2) overlaps a live loan's [0, 2) on exactly one byte is refused at Q078 naming the footprint that decided it, with the overlap decided at check time by max low < min high. The boundary control moves the byte outside both ranges and is admitted (CT07's own case shape at the wave-28 mapping; CT07's case is the write-lend program since card CT07-WRITE-REMAP); the attribution control runs the identical write with no live loan and is admitted. The `analyzer potential/unknown` arm is not claimed: Unknown remains the gateway's verdict vocabulary, and the source harness's is accept/reject.

cases.scenario: Distinct ordinary struct fields
cases.semantic_profile: StandardBufferV1 with source.record.v1 (card AGGREGATES-V1): three declared record fields constructed with three different check-time-constant values, all three read back and printed, plus a second value of the same type read in another order. The ACCESS proof is supplied - construction totality, projection soundness and distinctness are checked, and the bad_field control refuses a read outside the declaration at Q052 - but the LAYOUT leg is an executed sanitized byte-comparison OBSERVATION, not a proof (AGGREGATE-CT09-LAYOUT): that a C compiler's designated initializer and member reads agree with the model is cross-checked by the per-stream comparison of the case's own emitted C under ASan/UBSan/LSan, nothing proves it, and the proof stage stays unassessed. A record is a plain value of scalars with no custody; nothing here measures aggregates holding resources, nested aggregates, or concurrent field access.

cases.scenario: Protected owned graph grows/replaces identities
cases.semantic_profile: source.mutex.guard.v1 with card CT34-GROWTH's opt-in protection growth. CT34's scenario has two halves and this case separates them: a generation may GROW its protected footprint over memory nothing protects, and may never REPLACE an identity another generation already protects. Three resources are declared with generations over the first two; the case grows `m` onto `y`, which `n` already protects, and is refused at Q617 FootprintAlreadyProtected. The exact ordered cascade [Q613, Q617, Q619, Q613, Q600, Q600, Q600] is pinned and every entry says something: the section unlocks with its invariant still open (Q613 InvariantOpenAtUnlock), the growth's own refusal sits SECOND rather than first because the lowering mints the new predicate identity before the core decides (Q617; card boundary CT34-GROWTH-CASCADE, recorded rather than concealed), the generation is destroyed with its guard still live (Q619), the section's `close` names a declared identity the generation never took because the refused growth installed nothing (Q613 InvalidInvariantWitness), and scope exit finds the resource, the guard and the generation outstanding (three Q600). Every entry after Q617 is what shows the refusal left the generation's shape, its declared identity and the share ledger exactly as they were. The admitted control differs by exactly ONE TOKEN - the growth names the unprotected `z` instead of `y` - so the refusal is attributable to the interval already having a protector rather than to growth being written down at all. That control is `accept_growth`: the core admits it, records one admitted protection growth, and compile_files returns a compiled module carrying emitted C. Card CT34-SANITIZED retired card CT34-GROWTH's boundary 3 (CT34-GROWTH-NATIVE): the backend now renders a growth the certificate admits, as no mtx_t operation at all plus one bookkeeping line, because a footprint is a DECLARED SHAPE and a C mutex has no extent to widen; a growth no certificate admits is refused at UnadmittedProtectionGrowth. A second control grows onto the generation's OWN declared interval and refuses with the identical seven-entry cascade, so W4's one-protector rule is measured to cover this generation's shape too. There is no shrink or replacement form in this profile at all, and the unconditional Q618 fixed-shape refusal beside the growth is unchanged. Only parse, elaborate, mutex_lowering and mutex_invariant_check execute; this route emits from a checked event list and has no CFG stage. native_sanitized is executed and harness-gated: a third control, growth_then_guarded_access.qcore, writes the originally declared region under the guard, grows onto a second allocation, writes the newly protected region under the SAME guard and reads both in a second section; the harness compiles its emitted C under ASan/UBSan/LSan, runs it, and compares stdout line for line with interpret_mutex_program. The case's own fixture is a refusal that emits nothing, so the four native stages name that control's file as their artifact - the only file a compiler in this case ever saw - rather than case.qcore. The run witnesses in-bounds access to real allocations inside the growing section's own lock/unlock pair and full reclamation under LeakSanitizer; it witnesses NOTHING about a C mutex protecting the grown region, about contention, about any schedule, or about the invariant predicate.

cases.scenario: Stack capture expires or environment moves before join
cases.semantic_profile: ScopedReadLoansV1 (cards T05 and WRITE-LEND-TASKS) over the checked scoped-task ledger. CT44's scenario is `Stack capture expires or environment moves before join`, expected Reject, and the case is REFUSED with each word carried by a named rule of an unedited model except one, stated as a boundary below. CAPTURE by the checked task IR's own loan: the parent lends `read buffer share FULL` at the spawn and the refusal names the resource, the outstanding amount and the BORROWING TASK -- LoanOutstanding { resource: 1, outstanding: 1024, borrowers: [2] } -- which is the capture, not the handle, and is card T00's archived blocker for this case (`the available rejection is about the handle, not about a capture whose environment expires`) measured obsolete on this tree. EXPIRES by the written `drop buffer;` statement, whose executed meaning on this route is a real destruction: the identical program with that statement after the join is ADMITTED (drop_after_join.qcore, ScopedReadLoansV1). BEFORE JOIN because that relative position is exactly what moves the verdict, pinned in both directions -- the same destruction in the same position with a scalar capture instead of the buffer's share also checks (scalar_capture_drop.qcore, ScopedOwnedTasksV1), so the refusal is keyed to the capture and not to destroying while a child runs, nor to the position alone. OR ENVIRONMENT MOVES by the scenario's second disjunct, which has the source form card T00 recorded it lacked (`captures are copied into a checked environment, so environment moves before join has no source form` -- true at T00's checkpoint, where share captures did not lower at all, and false here): `move buffer` handing custody to a second worker while the first share is out, refused at the same Q600 LoanOutstanding, attributed to the moving statement (move_before_join.qcore). The frame's own expiry is pinned as a fourth control rather than as the case -- a bare return out of the thread scope with the share out, refused at Q600 ScopeBusy whose message names the frame -- because card CT-WIRE-LANE-3 (wave 31) recorded that the task route executes no destroy at scope exit, so the case is written instead on the statement whose executed meaning an admitting control demonstrates. BOUNDARY: the captured storage is a HEAP buffer bound to a parent-frame local; this language has no stack-allocated capturable resource, so `stack` has NO REFERENT and the case is mapped on the frame-owned-resource shape, on the CT06 precedent for an inexpressible vehicle. What carries the hazard is that `thread scope` IS the scoped-thread construct and the ledger refuses exactly the expiry or transfer of the captured resource before the join. No native, sanitizer or proof evidence is claimed: the fixture is a refusal that reaches no backend.

cases.scenario: Known shared wrapper with non-Sync but Send payload
cases.expected: Accept only through verified mutex protocol
cases.semantic_profile: CheckedMutexGuardsV1: a `protected N` payload -- the transferability judgment's TransferKind::ProtectedResource, sendable over a derivable synchronization edge and not freely shareable -- declared to cross into a child task under the generation that protects it (TransferMode::ShareUnderMutex requesting ShareProtocol::CheckedMutex), with every reach of the payload by either task naming a guard. Since card MUTEX-SHARE-CROSS-EMISSION (wave 36) the crossing also EXECUTES: the child is a real C11 thread that performs its own mtx_lock/mtx_unlock on the generation, and the emitted program's standard output is compared byte for byte under ASan/UBSan/LSan with interpret_mutex_program's observation of the same checked trace. The evidence is acquisition/release pairing across a real thread boundary and the validity of the protected allocation, on one Linux target. It is NOT evidence about contention or any data race: the checked trace is a total order whose child segment is contiguous, so the faithful rendering joins the child immediately and the creator performs no trace event while the child runs (MUTEX-SHARE-CROSS-EMISSION-NO-CONTENTION); no TSan row exists anywhere in this repository. CT46's own words `wrapper` and `non-Sync but Send` have no referent in this language and are carried by the judgment's classification instead; the task route's own own<Buffer> still cannot request mutex mediation (MUTEX-SHARE-CROSS-TASK-BUFFER).

cases.scenario: Raw pointer is Copy but no transfer/share contract exists
cases.semantic_profile: The transferability judgment (qcore_core::transfer, cards CT46-SENDSYNC and CT47-COPY-CAPTURE) over ScopedOwnedTasksV1's checked spawn boundary. CT47's scenario is `Raw pointer is Copy but no transfer/share contract exists`, expected `Reject automatic cross-thread acceptance`, and the case is REFUSED with each word carried by a named rule of an unedited model except one, stated as a boundary below. BUT NO TRANSFER/SHARE CONTRACT EXISTS by the judgment itself: the capture `spawn s reader(copy buffer)` is refused at Q600, attributed to the capture span at the crossing construct, with a message that names the missing contract and enumerates the three this kind does carry (`move`, `read PLACE share N`, `lend PLACE LOW..HIGH`). IS COPY at the MODE level: `copy` is this route's bit-duplication mode and the judgment classifies `own<Buffer>` as SENDABLE, so the refusal is for the mode and not a vacuous `this kind never crosses` -- the audited theorem QCore.Transferability.copyOfTheOwnedBufferIsRefusedForItsMode pins exactly that cell, and theBoundaryIsDecidedExactlyOnce pins that refusal and admission partition the whole 13 x 4 x 13 boundary matrix. REJECT AUTOMATIC ACCEPTANCE in two measured halves: the explicit request is refused by the judgment (the case), and the automatic form is not spellable at all -- a capture with no declared mode does not parse (Q000, the grammar, byte-identical to the wave-26 measurement), pinned as modeless.qcore. The attribution is complete rather than illustrative: all three contracts the message enumerates are supplied by accepted controls (move_transfer.qcore ScopedOwnedTasksV1, read_share.qcore ScopedReadSharesV1, write_lease.qcore ScopedWriteLeasesV1) and every one of them admits the program. BOUNDARIES: this language has no raw pointer type -- DeclaredTypeTag::Pointer is Unmodeled and a declared pointer parameter refuses long before a capture is considered -- so `raw pointer` has NO REFERENT and the bit-copy of an owned handle is the nearest expressible shape (the CT06 precedent, whose `same pointer` scenario is mapped on a {ptr, len} view with `pointer values the language gives no type remain outside this route` published in its own profile). Relatedly, no QCore type is both freely duplicable and resource-bearing, because resource kinds are linear, so the dangerous COMBINATION the scenario names is prevented by the type system and this fixture demonstrates the rule at the boundary rather than the combination itself. Before card CT47-COPY-CAPTURE (wave 29) this same shape fell through to the C backend's Q500 executable-subset catch-all, which is why the wave-26 CT lane measured it and declined to map. No native, sanitizer or proof evidence is claimed for this artifact: the fixture is a refusal that reaches no backend, and the Lean theorems prove the model's judgment rather than this case's fixture (T00.7 stays open; proof stays 3 of 45).

cases.scenario: Stale heap refinement reused after mutex release/reacquire
cases.semantic_profile: source.mutex.guard.v1 with card T03-F's guard-scoped facts: a refinement established under one guard and relied on under a later acquisition of the same mutex is refused at Q616 StaleProtectedFact, cascade exactly [Q616] because the release that dropped the fact was itself well formed. Both directions of the spec's invalidate/re-establish expectation execute: the reasserted control re-establishes the fact under the second guard and is accepted; the never_asserted control refuses at Q600 UnknownFact, so Q616 is staleness rather than absence. The binder is declared at thread-scope level so the name resolves and the model refuses the use, which is the semantic refusal the T03 CT integration report recorded the weaker Q013 unknown-name refusal as insufficient for. Only parser and type_checker execute; cfg is unassessed (no CFG stage). Not established: a fact has no predicate, so this is refinement invalidation and not refinement content. The reasserted control is single-task and does emit C, but the harness route-checks it rather than running it; evidence_target records the Q500 host gate.

cases.scenario: Independent event order differs between C and interpreter
cases.expected: Validate partial order, not exact total trace
cases.semantic_profile: ComposedStdIoTasksV1 (source.std-io-tasks.v1) with a source line in a worker body, so the declared observation relation is qcore.obs-reordering.v1 rather than byte equality. The emitted program performs each worker's lines on that worker's own thread; the reference execution runs each worker eagerly at its spawn; and the two are compared window by window and emitter by emitter on standard error while standard output stays byte-compared. Linux ASan/UBSan/LSan. Nothing here is a claim about the scheduler: an admitted run says that run's stream lies in the admitted set.

cases.scenario: New lifetime reuses old numeric address/descriptor
cases.expected: Old capability cannot authorize new identity
cases.semantic_profile: Linux ScopedOwnedTasksV1 Buffer lifetime identity: two successful root allocations are separated by real munmap/mmap at the same numeric address using MAP_FIXED_NOREPLACE. Native release hooks check generations 1 and 2, exact mapping identity and complete release. Stale read/drop of the first consumed binding after the new allocation reject at Q600. Native stdout agrees with reference generation events. This covers owned Buffer mappings, not arbitrary raw pointers, descriptors, allocator failures or full source/native refinement.
